svg.title: LES DC-3 hydraulic system as simulated: reservoir, two engine pumps, hand pump, regulator, accumulator, and the five services
svg.desc: Simplified block diagram of the simulated DC-3 hydraulic system. Top left, the reservoir: 2.5 US gallons of MIL-H-5606 with a sight glass on its side that shows the fill less what is out in the circuits. The engine pumps draw through a standpipe that ends above a 0.75 gallon hand pump reserve at the bottom, so they starve once the fill is down in the reserve; the hand pump draws from the bottom of the tank. Every return line comes back to the top of the reservoir. Two engine-driven pumps, 3 gallons a minute at 1400 rpm and up to 875 psi, output following rpm, feed the pump selector valve on the cockpit floor: NORMAL sends both pumps to the system, ALTERNATE sends the right pump to the Sperry A-3A servos, the Classic's gyropilot, through the autopilot shutoff valve, which the gyropilot will not engage across when closed, and leaves the left pump alone carrying the system. From the selector the flow goes through the pressure regulator, cut-in 650 psi and cut-out 875, whose bypass above 875 returns to the reservoir, then past the system relief valve, which opens at 1000 psi to the reservoir, and on to the pressure manifold at 650 to 875 psi, which every service draws from. The system pressure gauge reads the manifold: 650 to 875 running, 50 more a hand pump stroke. The hand pump between the seats, double-acting at about 50 psi a stroke, feeds the manifold through its own shutoff valve, open to pump and closed in flight. The accumulator hangs on the manifold with an air precharge of 250 psi over 0.15 US gallons of fluid, which shows in the sight glass; a thermal relief valve at 950 psi protects the 0.5 gallon zone that is trapped once the pumps stop. Five services draw from the manifold through a distribution bar. Landing gear: the control valve, UP, NEUTRAL and DOWN, after the lock lever and safety latch, with solenoids blocking UP on the ground, feeds three actuators of 0.12 US gallons each; the landing gear pressure gauge reads the circuit past the valve, holds after a cycle and bleeds on an actuator seal failure; a thermal relief at 1000 psi protects 0.3 gallons trapped; below 100 psi the gear falls of its own weight. Wing flaps: the control valve, UP, NEUTRAL and DOWN, moves the flaps above 500 psi and traps the fluid in NEUTRAL to hold them; the actuator holds 0.08 US gallons and takes 14 seconds for full travel; the flap relief valve of 430 to 485 psi exists in the simulation only as a failure, stuck open; with no pressure in flight the air loads blow the flaps up, in Veteran only. Wheel brakes: the power brake control valve on the pedals passes up to 875 psi to the left and right brakes, which bite at 100 psi and are full at 875; the parking brake latches the line and needs 100 psi to set and none to release; each brake line has a thermal relief at 750 psi over 0.1 gallons. Cowl flaps: two control valves, left and right, OFF, CLOSE, TRAIL and OPEN, branch off the brake supply and each drives a double-acting strut above 400 psi, 8 seconds at 875; OFF locks the strut and TRAIL lets it float; each carries an integral relief at 1150 psi over 0.15 gallons. Windshield wipers: valves, OFF, LOW and HIGH, one a side, drive one motor a side; they need 400 psi to move and their speed follows the pressure. All five relief valves vent to the reservoir. A dot marks lines that are joined; a crossing without a dot is not. Simplified, as simulated; Chapter 9.
